races.paceDynamic: Alliteration is the lone confirmed front runner in this 18-runner field and should get an uncontested lead, having shown the ability to sustain her effort when making the running in previous starts. The prominent runners like Salsinha, Poetic Twist, Cool Native and Simply Natural will likely settle just behind but none are natural pace pressers. This creates a scenario where Alliteration can dictate terms without being harassed early, then the race will develop into a staying test up the hill at Fairyhouse on soft ground. This race shape strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can position close to the pace, as hold-up horses will struggle to make up ground in the testing conditions with such a large field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Runner Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Alliteration gets an easy lead and maintains her rhythm throughout
scenarios.body: She can dictate the fractions and prove hard to peg back up the hill, having shown consistent form when allowed to lead. Her natural front-running style perfectly suits getting first run on this large field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes too sedate and prominent runners can quicken
scenarios.body: The likes of Salsinha and Poetic Twist can use their class to sweep past a tiring leader in the final furlong. Their higher ratings and tactical speed become decisive factors.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely strong and the field comes back to the closers
scenarios.body: Horses like Simply Natural or Shesakindofmagic can time their runs perfectly as front runners tire. The soft ground aids their staying power in a truly-run race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Benefits Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If market leaders make errors or the pace becomes stop-start
scenarios.body: A lesser-fancied runner like Brosna Queen can benefit from a messy race where class doesn't tell. Experience and a good position become more valuable than raw ability.

races.paceDynamic: Bioluminescence will lead from the start with no serious pace pressure, allowing her to dictate fractions and jump in rhythm. The prominently-raced quartet of Mystical Goddess, Broomfield Bijou, Kilbarry Saint and May Call You Back will track within striking distance but none are natural pace forcers. This creates a tactical race where the tempo builds gradually after halfway, suiting horses who can quicken from prominent positions rather than those needing to come from the back. The sustained gallop and soft ground favour prominent racers and strong stayers over hold-up horses who rely on turn of foot.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bioluminescence Controls All
scenarios.trigger: If the leader jumps fluently and faces no early pressure from the prominent pack.
scenarios.body: Her class tells as she uses tactical advantage to string out the field, with prominent racers best placed to respond when the pace lifts. Hold-up horses struggle to make up ground on the testing surface.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Develops
scenarios.trigger: If Mystical Goddess or Kilbarry Saint press forward to challenge the leader approaching halfway.
scenarios.body: The increased tempo plays into the hands of those tracking just behind, creating a war of attrition that exposes any stamina doubts. Strong travellers in the prominent group can capitalise on a pace collapse.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is slower than expected and the soft ground doesn't drain stamina reserves.
scenarios.body: This allows the back markers time to organise their challenge, with Me Wee Bonnie Lass and Ballybawn Belter getting first run on tiring leaders. The race becomes about who has the best finishing kick.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Bioluminescence stops quickly and the prominent group tie up on the testing ground.
scenarios.body: The race opens up for any horse still travelling, regardless of early position, with stamina becoming the decisive factor. Patient rides on proven stayers can capitalise on a messy finish.

races.paceDynamic: Lord Lariat and Dancing Jeremy are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead, with Dancing Jeremy having shown more recent form and likely to take them along at a solid gallop. The honest pace will stretch the field over this 2m5f trip on testing ground, creating a stamina test rather than a sprint finish. With 17 runners and two keen leaders ensuring no crawl, this shape strongly favours prominent racers and hold-up horses who can stay the trip, while pure speed horses will struggle in the conditions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Gallop Grind
scenarios.trigger: If Dancing Jeremy and Lord Lariat maintain a solid early gallop without going crazy fast...
scenarios.body: The testing ground and sustained pace will find out the weak stayers, setting up perfectly for battle-hardened hold-up horses who can grind past tiring leaders. Horses like Dutch Schultz and Lucky Lyreen thrive in these tactical scenarios where class and stamina combine.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Lord Lariat's long absence tells early and Dancing Jeremy gets an easy lead...
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the last mile with fresh horses swooping late, favouring the best natural speed from off the pace. Prominent runners who can quicken will have the edge over pure plodders.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina Slog Battle
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground really takes its toll and multiple horses tire in the straight...
scenarios.body: This becomes a war of attrition where only the strongest stayers survive, heavily favouring horses proven over longer trips. The marathon specialists will pick up the pieces as classier but less robust horses fade.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Leaders Dominate Home
scenarios.trigger: If Dancing Jeremy finds this trip ideal and gets into a rhythm without serious pressure...
scenarios.body: The front-runner can dictate terms completely and prove hard to peg back, with only the most prominent runners able to mount a challenge. Early positioning becomes crucial as the field strings out.

races.paceDynamic: This shapes as a truly searching gallop with confirmed front runners Petit Secret, Sine Qua Non, and He Can't Dance all committed to leading, creating genuine pressure from the outset. The strong pace will stretch the field over 2m4f on soft ground, with the stamina-sapping conditions likely to find out the inexperienced debutants who make up half this field. The relentless gallop will set up perfectly for hold-up horses and prominent racers with proven stamina who can pick up the pieces. This race shape decisively favours patient, staying types who can finish strongly when the pace-setters weaken.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the three confirmed leaders go too hard early and crack from two out
scenarios.body: The strong gallop will stretch the field but ultimately undo the pace-setters, allowing hold-up horses with proven stamina to sweep past tired leaders. Patient tactics and finishing kick become decisive on the testing soft ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Strike
scenarios.trigger: If one prominent runner can sit just off the pace without getting involved in the early battle
scenarios.body: A horse like Treasure Memory or Midnight Jet can track the leaders without burning energy, then strike when the front three weaken. Their experience advantage over the debutants becomes crucial in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Survives Strong Pace
scenarios.trigger: If He Can't Dance can dictate a more manageable tempo despite the other pace-setters
scenarios.body: His proven hurdling experience and Gordon Elliott stable strength allows him to control the race better than his front-running rivals. The soft ground suits his record and he has the class to withstand pressure.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutant Surprise Package
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed newcomers has been well-schooled and handles the occasion
scenarios.body: A horse like Barnpark or one of the Henry De Bromhead pair could have been specifically prepared for this target. Their lack of form could mask genuine ability that emerges under race conditions.

watchPoints.text: If He Can't Dance gets into an early speed duel with Petit Secret and Sine Qua Non, all three could compromise their chances and set up the race for closers
Watch for any of the Henry De Bromhead debutants (Glenary Prince, Midnight Jet) showing unexpected early pace, as this could indicate hidden ability
Monitor how Largy Star and Siege Of Carthage are travelling turning for home, as both hold-up horses are perfectly positioned to benefit from pace collapse
Keep an eye on Treasure Memory's positioning - if he can sit closer than usual without getting involved in the pace battle, his experience becomes a major asset
Watch for any of the Gordon Elliott outsiders (Le Questionnaire) making unexpected moves, as the stable's confidence could be with their second string rather than the obvious choice

races.paceDynamic: Six confirmed front runners (Hens Tooth, Star Of The Week, Daydream Nation, Panjandrum, Blow Wind Blow, Fou De Toi) guarantee a strong gallop from the start in this 21-runner field. The pace will be relentless early, with multiple horses vying for the lead, before the 3m trip and soft ground combine to test stamina reserves over the final mile. Those prominent early like Court Compliance and Vitorio Piel will be perfectly positioned as the leaders tire, while hold-up horses face a significant task getting competitive from the rear in such a large field. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track the pace without leading, positioning them to strike as the genuine gallop takes its toll.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace leaders go too fast early and multiple front runners fade from 2f out
scenarios.body: Court Compliance and Vitorio Piel can track the strong gallop without leading, perfectly positioned to strike as Daydream Nation and Star Of The Week tire. The relentless early pace sets up ideal conditions for horses racing in second or third to take over.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the large field spreads out and the pace becomes more moderate than expected
scenarios.body: Gin Tonic and Found A Diamond can use their staying power to weave through traffic and mount late challenges. Despite the strong early pace, class horses can still pick up the pieces if positioned well by their jockeys.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one pace-setter finds the perfect rhythm and the field doesn't close them down effectively
scenarios.body: Daydream Nation or Blow Wind Blow could steal a march by finding their own tempo early while others fight for position. Their recent form over similar trips suggests they can sustain a strong gallop to the line.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Benefits From Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and multiple fancied horses get into trouble
scenarios.body: Chase The Moon or Tip Of The Wings could benefit from a truly-run race where stamina becomes paramount over ratings. The large field and soft ground create opportunities for unfancied horses with the right trip credentials.

runners_data.comment: Cheltenham also-ran hampered here previously; Walsh prefers Davy Crockett
runners_data.spotlight: Last season's Fred Winter winner at Cheltenham never threatened on return there last month in 2m5f Coral Cup; previously hampered at least twice when well held behind Zillow over today's C&D; Walsh prefers Davy Crockett.

runners_data.name: Sony Bill

runners_data.spotlight: Two hurdle wins in France in spring 2024; yet to score for Willie Mullins in six attempts but set some stiff tasks, most recently didn't seem to stay 2m5f of Coral Cup at Cheltenham; return to 2m may suit but yard look to have stronger contenders.

runners_data.name: Murcia
runners_data.note: Prominent Grade 1 winner, fine fourth to Bowensonfire shows current form
runners_data.comment: Didn't count in County Hurdle latest but can't be discounted on DRF run previously
runners_data.spotlight: Won a Grade 1 juvenile hurdle at Aintree last year; lightly raced this season, but DRF fourth of 19 to Bowensonfire in 2m handicap was a fine run; didn't count in County Hurdle latest but can't be discounted.

runners_data.name: Messerschmitt
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with 5lb claimer, encouraging return from winter break last time

runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't added to Galway 3yo maiden win although last month's return from winter break was encouraging, not fluent last when fourth of 18 behind Mondo Man in Imperial Cup at Sandown; runs off same mark here, rider's claim a positive.

runners_data.name: Lord Erskine
runners_data.note: 13yo hold-up horse defending champion off 9lb higher mark, returning from break
runners_data.comment: Last year's winner now a 13yo and needs a career-best to follow up
runners_data.spotlight: Fine dual-purpose performer won this last year (beating Helvic Dream) off 9lb lower; won twice on Flat afterwards, back from a break when well held back over hurdles at DRF in February; 13yo probably needs a career-best over hurdles to follow up here.

runners_data.name: Mode Avion
runners_data.note: 4yo prominent runner improving with cheekpieces, won at this C&D in February
runners_data.comment: Progressive 4yo could go well off light weight

runners_data.name: Davy Crockett
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse related to Mystical Power, won first three starts before recent defeats

runners_data.name: Zillow
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with 7lb claimer, both wins over 2m but struggled off higher marks
runners_data.comment: C&D winner in November hasn't stayed 2m5f twice since; cheekpieces added and drops in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Both hurdles wins over 2m, including Listed handicap here in November; has struggled off revised mark since however, twice not looking to stay 2m5f, latest in Martin Pipe at Cheltenham; return to 2m in his favour and cheekpieces tried.

runners_data.name: Putapoundinthejar

runners_data.comment: Ground at DRF wouldn't have suited; potential improver on better ground
runners_data.spotlight: Two hurdle wins last term came at 2m, including Punchestown handicap off 117; quiet enough hurdles campaign this season, lots to find on latest DRF effort (heavy); better ground will suit.

runners_data.name: Missus Beeton

runners_data.comment: Hat-trick seeker has 19lb rise to overcome and 2lb wrong; still respected

runners_data.name: Playtime
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won last time over hurdles despite racing keenly
runners_data.comment: Leopardstown maiden winner would appreciate ground drying on handicap debut

runners_data.name: Powerful

runners_data.comment: Dual Punchestown winner likes going right-handed; 8lb higher after a break
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark on handicap debut over this trip at Punchestown in November (heavy) and returned there on latest nicely improved to win over 2m5f in January; had a break since and reverts to 2m off 8lb higher mark.

runners_data.name: Kotkito Bello

runners_data.spotlight: On a roll earlier in the season, hat-trick of wins included over hurdles at Punchestown and Thurles; DRF fifth wasn't a bad run upped in grade but other may now be better handicapped (1lb wrong here).

runners_data.name: Kalix Delabarriere
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with 7lb claimer but very poor recent handicap form, hard to fancy
runners_data.comment: Pulled up after never counting at DRF; cheekpieces added but very hard to be confident in
runners_data.spotlight: Bumper and maiden hurdle winner but has been poor on last three starts in handicaps, pulled up after never counting at DRF in February; cheekpieces added but very hard to be confident in (1lb wrong).

runners_data.name: Bokamsin
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse improving in tongue-tie, made all to win at Navan last time
runners_data.comment: Much improved in tongue-tie to dominate at Navan; opening mark seems okay
runners_data.spotlight: Nicely improved on fifth attempt hurdling to land 2m Navan novice last month, making all in beating Tip Of The Wings (runs in 4.25) 6l in first-time tongue-tie; unlikely he'll be able to dominate in same way here but progressive and opening mark seems okay.

races.paceDynamic: Kotkito Bello is the only confirmed front runner in this 19-runner field and should get an uncontested lead, setting a sustainable pace without early pressure. The prominent runners like Puturhandstogether, Sony Bill, Murcia, Mode Avion and Playtime will track but won't challenge for the early lead. With 13 hold-up horses including Hello Neighbour, Karbau, Helvic Dream and Sea Of Sands all needing room late, the finish will be a cavalry charge from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can position handily behind the lone leader and kick for home before the hold-up brigade gets organized.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent trackers position perfectly behind Kotkito Bello and kick before the final furlong
scenarios.body: They'll have first run on the hold-up horses who need time to organize in a big field, with the soft ground helping stamina types. The 13 hold-up horses will struggle for racing room and clean runs in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Heroes Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly pedestrian and the hold-up horses get clean runs through
scenarios.body: The class horses like Karbau and Hello Neighbour will have devastating finishing kicks on the soft ground. Their superior ratings will tell once they find daylight in the final 200 yards.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Lasts
scenarios.trigger: If Kotkito Bello gets too easy a lead and the field leaves their run too late
scenarios.body: His three wins earlier this season show he stays strongly, and the soft ground will sap the finishing kicks of those behind. The 62-day break may have freshened him up perfectly for a bold front-running display.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Kotkito Bello goes too slow early then stops, creating a messy finish with traffic problems
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery with horses coming from all angles in the final furlong. Any horse with luck in running and a turn of foot could prevail in the scramble.

watchPoints.text: Watch for traffic problems late with 13 hold-up horses needing room in the final 2 furlongs
Monitor if Kotkito Bello gets too easy a lead early, could steal a march on this big field
Keep an eye on the prominent trackers like Murcia and Puturhandstogether positioning behind the leader
Watch for Karbau and Hello Neighbour getting squeezed for room given their hold-up styles in this big field
Observe if the 62-day breaks for Sea Of Sands, Lord Erskine and Kotkito Bello show rustiness or freshness

runners_data.spotlight: Poet's Word sister to 1m-1m4f AW winner Trishuli River and half-sister to Italian hurdle winner Natris; winning debut in Down Royal mares' bumper last month, seeing it out well under strong handling; more needed but possible.

runners_data.name: Lilannbee
runners_data.note: Lone front runner who won when leading at Punchestown but vulnerable if pace becomes tactical

runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark at fourth attempt when allowed to dictate at Punchestown in December (yielding); out of depth in Grade 2 mares' event at DRF since; more exposed than several of these.

runners_data.name: Something Fabulous
runners_data.note: Classy winner returning from 174-day break with solid prominent style to exploit controlled tempo
runners_data.comment: Tramore winner back from winter break with hood fitted; probably wants better ground
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark in second bumper, nicking it before the home turn at Tramore in August (good); two months later didn't get home as well over 2m3f at Cork when third; back from winter break with hood fitted; probably wants better ground.

runners_data.name: Belladaball
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who finished fourth to Lizzie Twigg last time, needs significant improvement
runners_data.comment: Respectable efforts both here and at Down Royal in February; more needed
runners_data.spotlight: Respectable efforts both here and at Down Royal (fourth to Lizzie Twigg) in February when ridden handier; more needed.

runners_data.name: Some Pretender
runners_data.note: Listed-class prominent runner returning from 139-day absence, proven in soft ground conditions
runners_data.comment: Decent efforts in similar events of late; should be thereabouts
runners_data.spotlight: Had two subsequent winners behind when justifying favouritism at Galway on debut in August (2m1f, good); stiffer task since in Listed mares' events on much softer ground, decent third at Gowran and front-running third to a warm favourite at Navan (second narrowly beaten in Grade 2 afterwards), racing a bit keen; entitled to be thereabouts, especially if settling better.

runners_data.name: Moyneard
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning from 27-day break after staying-on second at Thurles, suited by tactical race
runners_data.comment: Steady pace may not have suited at Naas; may yet improve, especially in a truly-run race

runners_data.name: Wonderful Everyday
runners_data.note: High-class hold-up mare whose recent form is concerning but race shape could unlock ability
runners_data.comment: Sets the standard on her Punchestown form but hard to be confident in on recent efforts

runners_data.name: Voladora Nora
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning from 168-day winter break, needs major improvement to feature prominently
runners_data.comment: Listowel third returns from winter break and needs to improve plenty to feature
runners_data.spotlight: Pick of three bumper efforts when third at Listowel; back from winter break and needs to improve plenty to feature.

races.paceDynamic: Lilannbee is the only confirmed front runner and will dictate from the start without pressure, having successfully led at Punchestown when winning. The prominent group of Lizzie Twigg, Something Fabulous, Some Pretender and Belladaball will track her but none are habitual pace pressers. This creates a controlled tempo that allows the hold-up horses Wonderful Everyday and Moyneard to get into contention, while the sustainable pace should favour those who can quicken from mid-pack positions. The lack of pace pressure strongly favours prominent trackers and hold-up horses over the lone leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Lilannbee sets uncontested fractions and the prominent horses get first run
scenarios.body: The controlled pace allows prominent runners to conserve energy and quicken decisively approaching the finish. Lizzie Twigg's recent winning form or Something Fabulous's class edge become decisive factors when the race opens up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow and the finish becomes a sprint
scenarios.body: The tactical race setup perfectly suits the patient hold-up runners who can unleash late kicks. Wonderful Everyday's class from her Punchestown win or Moyneard's recent staying-on form at Thurles becomes the winning factor.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Lasts Home
scenarios.trigger: If Lilannbee gets easy early fractions and the others leave their runs too late
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader builds enough advantage through steady sectionals to resist late challenges on the testing ground. Her Punchestown victory showed she can sustain when allowed to control the tempo from the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Package Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes truly run to suit an outsider's specific profile
scenarios.body: The tactical nature and small field create opportunities for horses whose recent form doesn't reflect their ability in these conditions. The pace collapse suits a horse who can find extra when the race opens up late.

watchPoints.text: Wonderful Everyday must show early signs of her old ability or her poor recent form suggests deeper issues
Lilannbee's jockey tactics early - if pressured by prominent runners, her stamina reserves become questionable
Something Fabulous adapting quickly to race fitness after 174-day layoff in this competitive Listed contest
Moyneard's positioning through halfway - if too far back, the controlled pace may not provide enough late acceleration
Lizzie Twigg's jumping off quickly to secure ideal tracking position behind the likely uncontested leader
